summary.title: A Guide to Seed Fundraising
summary.one_liner: You learn the basics of raising a startup's first (seed) round: when and how much to raise, safes versus convertible notes versus equity, valuation, meeting investors, closing, and the documents you need.
keywords: how much should a startup raise
when should a startup raise money
takeaways: Raise when you have a clear market, a product with real adoption (traction), and a believable plan; raise enough to reach the next fundable milestone, often 12 to 18 months out.
Estimate round size from monthly cost per engineer (about $15k all-in, per the guide) times headcount times months of runway.
Seed rounds in Silicon Valley are mostly done as SAFEs or convertible notes; a SAFE drops the interest rate and maturity, and equity rounds are more complex and costly.
Walk through the dilution math: a $1M raise on a $5M pre-money valuation gives about 16.7% dilution, not 20%.
Get warm introductions, optimize for getting the first money soon, and close quickly using standard documents such as the YC safe.
summary.summary: This Y Combinator guide summarizes what startup founders need to know about raising a seed round. It covers why startups need outside capital, when to raise, how much to raise (including a runway-based estimate and typical dilution ranges), and the main financing instruments: convertible debt, the SAFE, and priced equity. It also explains valuation, the differences between angels and VCs, crowdfunding, meeting investors, negotiating and closing, and the documents to prepare, such as an executive summary and a 12-part pitch deck outline. The author draws on experience at startups, YC, and Imagine K12, and the page links to further reading by Paul Graham and others.
